root_cause.text: The IPMI SSIF probe path created a kthread before the interface was fully registered, but the error cleanup path failed to stop and clear that thread when `ssif_probe()` aborted before `ipmi_register_smi()` installed the normal shutdown handler, leaving a running thread behind.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds explicit `kthread_stop(ssif_info->thread); ssif_info->thread = NULL;` in the `ssif_probe()` error path and notes that “If `ipmi_register_smi()` starts the interface, it will call shutdown and that will free the thread and set it to NULL. Otherwise it must be freed here,” while `shutdown_ssif()` is also updated to NULL the thread after stopping it.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop the SSIF thread and clear its pointer during shutdown to avoid leaving a stale thread reference behind.
intent_record.what: In `shutdown_ssif()`, the single-line `if (ssif_info->thread) kthread_stop(ssif_info->thread);` was expanded into a block, and after stopping the thread the code now assigns `ssif_info->thread = NULL;`.
intent_record.how: After the worker thread is stopped, the stored thread pointer is explicitly cleared so later code will no longer treat it as an active thread handle. This prevents stale pointer reuse and makes the shutdown state more accurate.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix probe failure cleanup by stopping and releasing the SSIF thread when initialization does not complete.
intent_record.what: In the ssif_probe() error path, the code now checks whether ssif_info->thread is non-NULL and, if so, calls kthread_stop(ssif_info->thread) and sets ssif_info->thread to NULL before clearing addr_info->client.
intent_record.how: This ensures that a worker thread created during probe is explicitly stopped and released when probe fails, unless it has already been shut down elsewhere by ipmi_register_smi(); this prevents leaking the thread and avoids leaving a dangling thread pointer after an unsuccessful initialization.

bic_trace_step.reason: Yes, the snippet shows the exact probe/error path and the thread creation. In ssif_probe(), the driver starts the kthread before registration: `ssif_info->thread = kthread_run(ipmi_ssif_thread, ssif_info, ...)` and on failure paths after that it goes to `out:` where it only does `if (rv) kfree(ssif_info);` and `kfree(resp); return rv;`. There is no stop/cleanup of `ssif_info->thread` in the `goto out;` error path, unlike the remove path which later does `ssif_info->stopping = true; ... if (ssif_info->thread) { complete(&ssif_info->wake_thread); kthread_stop(ssif_info->thread); }`. This means the vulnerable construct is present: a thread can be created before the interface is fully registered, and aborting before `ipmi_register_smi()` succeeds can leave the thread running. The fix is not present in this commit because the probe error cleanup never stops or clears the thread before freeing `ssif_info`.
